quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: In good conditions, what is the minimum distance you should keep between you and the vehicle ahead?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: What vest or jacket color makes you most visible?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be seen. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: When it is raining, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, wet pavement is slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars because oil from other vehicles has not yet washed away. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to go.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve, apply light pressure to the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Switch between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, use the high beam.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: Try to move onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: The center of your lane is safest when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to cut back into your lane too early.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride only on it for better traction.
Avoid the entire center part of the lane.
Do not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of each lane. When the road is dry, this strip still provides enough grip for your motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to either side of it and still be in the center of your lane. Avoid it when wet.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride it out.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release and re-engage the front brake right away.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release and re-engage the front brake right away.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely and right away. Then apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid danger on a wet road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needs a lot of grip.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs strong grip to do safely. Do not swerve suddenly on wet surfaces.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required only for riders under age 18.
Only required when it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required only for riders under age 18.
questions.explanation: In Arizona, all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 18 must wear a helmet that is properly fastened.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move to the outside of the curve, then to the inside, before straightening out.

questions.question: When braking on a wet surface, you should:

options.text: Not use any brakes, but downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a wet surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when leaning than when upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes smoothly and gently.

questions.question: If taking a long trip, you should:

options.text: Try to take as few breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than 6 hours a day and take breaks every 2 hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine, as tiredness gets worse when they wear off.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually as bright as car headlights.
Usually not as bright as car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as bright as car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less bright than car headlights.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and increase pressure gradually.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and increase pressure gradually.
questions.explanation: To apply the front brake, squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers, applying pressure smoothly and steadily.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Maximum straight-line braking happens when you fully apply both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Because they are small, motorcycles may seem to be:

options.text: Going faster than they really are.
Going slower than they really are.
Not moving when they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they really are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles may look like they are going faster than they actually are.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil deposits that make it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also, slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular checks are an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding on warm days?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes. Riding jackets are designed to keep riders cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. Riding jackets are designed to keep riders cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket prevents dehydration and protects you in warm weather. Many jackets are designed to protect riders against overheating.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the roadway, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible before hitting the obstacle. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: What collects in the center portion of a traffic lane?

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from cars
The safest place for motorcycle riders to travel
Areas where drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from cars
questions.explanation: Debris and oil drippings from cars collect in the center of the lane. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also found there.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, and cold. They should also provide protection in case of a crash.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No lane position should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No lane position should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or always bad. Choose the lane position that matches your riding conditions.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it will block horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage over time, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still allowing you to hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing another vehicle on the left. This gives you a better view of oncoming traffic and makes you more visible.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction opposite of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction after you clear the hazard.
